solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inhabitants in location work with university

indicators.note: 'in' says the following pieces sit inside the word for a location

parts.note: a location is a place
OP, short for opus, is a work
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A census note about residents living near where some university work is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inhabitants in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the wordplay, putting the work and university inside the location.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general body of people who live in a place, its residents.

clue.text: Ecstatic journalist coming round at the last minute?

indicators.note: the journalist comes round, so wraps around the other piece

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
something done at the last minute is late

explanation.surface: A thrilled reporter who only showed up at the eleventh hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that being late is only one sense of doing something at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated and ecstatic are both synonyms for being in very high spirits.

clue.text: Software to take up and assess

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
to raise something is to take it up or lift it

explanation.surface: Instructions to adopt a new program and then evaluate it.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is a synonym for judging or estimating the worth of something.

clue.text: When descending on Kansas makes requests

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece descending on another sits directly above it in the column

parts.note: 'as' can mean when, as in 'as I left'
KS is the US postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Someone landing in Kansas, perhaps by parachute, who makes demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to make a request, so the third-person form matches the verb phrase.

clue.text: Nothing turned up in extra subtitle?

indicators.note: 'in' places the first piece inside the word for an extra

parts.note: in cricket a bye is an extra, a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a blank in some additional caption counts as a subtitle.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, and a bye is one kind. The question mark flags that a byline is only loosely a subtitle.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the secondary line under a newspaper headline naming the writer, a kind of subheading.

clue.text: Maybe start race, we hear, to provide pudding ingredient

indicators.note: we hear means the answer matches the sound of the phrase spoken

parts.note: a starter might say 'go' to begin a race

explanation.surface: An odd image of a race starter who somehow supplies an ingredient for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith used in milk puddings, a staple of British school dinners.

clue.text: Arch at entrance to large amphitheatre?

parts.note: a bow is an arch or curve

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of large

explanation.surface: An archway forming the entrance to a big open-air arena.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a bowl is an amphitheatre only by example, as in the Hollywood Bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a sloping stadium or outdoor theatre shaped like a basin, much like an amphitheatre.

clue.text: Kitty taken from cup stays out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and reset

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A collection of money withdrawn from a trophy that is not being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a pool of money linked to the cup; it is the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitty and pussycat are both affectionate names for a cat.

clue.text: Grub in tea urn, oddly, and a musical instrument!

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on of these four words

explanation.surface: An absurd picture of food stuck in a tea urn alongside a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection runs across all four words together, not just the tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a stringed instrument that is plucked or strummed.

clue.text: Small swine turned to tap on barrel

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a swine is a pig

indicators.note: turned means the short word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: A piglet that wandered over to the tap on a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or tap fitted to a cask to draw off liquid.

clue.text: Unhappy, coming across last of uneaten stuff on beach

indicators.note: one word coming across another spans it, so it wraps around

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of uneaten

explanation.surface: Someone glum at finding leftover food lying on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is the granular material covering most beaches.

clue.text: Tonsil, ear, sinus, back: that's too much for certain people!

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read from right to left
the clue words hold too many letters, so only a run inside them is wanted

parts.note: the letters running from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A patient complaining that tonsils, ears, sinuses and a back problem are all too much to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like one more ailment in the list; it is the instruction to read the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Israelis are citizens of Israel, a particular national group of people.

clue.text: Some appearing to need air when called?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: Some people showing up apparently in need of fresh air when summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like breathing space; it means a tune, and 'called' means phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtone is the short tune a mobile phone plays when someone calls it.

clue.text: Ale Basil ordered for girl

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged afresh into a new sequence

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Basil buying a beer for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a person, but his name is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a female first name, and crosswords often define a name by its gender.

clue.text: Agree pen needs to change colour

indicators.note: the letters must change their order to form the answer

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pen that agrees it must switch to a different ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green shade, named after peas.

clue.text: State oil's coming from mouth?

indicators.note: something coming from the mouth is spoken, so the word is judged by sound

parts.note: oil is grease, and the 's means 'oil is'

explanation.surface: A government complaining about oil spilling out of an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a verb meaning say; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a sovereign country, and a state is a nation.

clue.text: Sailing vessel, round, found in sports club

indicators.note: found in places the round letter inside the sports club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport, as in cricket
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A yacht belonging to a sports club that has been out on a round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Sports club reads as a members' society; it is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is any vessel for travelling on water, including one under sail.

clue.text: Accommodation on ship, we hear, for these new arrivals

indicators.note: we hear means the answer is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: berths are sleeping places on a ship

explanation.surface: Cabins arranged on a ship for newcomers boarding the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: New arrivals sound like passengers; they are babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Births are the arrivals of newborn babies into the world.

clue.text: Sailor's English books missing

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, plus the S of the possessive
E abbreviates English
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A sailor finds his English textbooks have gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent and missing are synonyms for not present.

clue.text: Reverberation upset grand toff

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a nob is a toff, an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman rattled by a loud echo.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff and a nob are both British slang for a posh person; a grand is a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is the deep ringing sound of a bell or gong, which reverberates.

clue.text: Peg must catch right plane, for example

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: Someone called Peg who has to catch the correct flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane looks like an aircraft; it is the plane tree, common in London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a kind of tree, so a tree is what a plane is an example of.

clue.text: Dull routine reflected essential Christmas tradition

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unchanging routine
key means essential or crucial

explanation.surface: Musing that a tedious routine is part of the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast turkey is the customary centrepiece of a British Christmas dinner, so it is a tradition.

clue.text: Corn seen waving, displayed by monitor

indicators.note: waving corn moves about, so the letters are moved around too

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Crops swaying in the breeze, shown on a video feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on screen is shown on a display such as a computer monitor.

clue.text: Mound close to church one's going to

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of church
I'll, short for I will, says one is going to do something

explanation.surface: An earthwork next to the church that someone intends to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill is a raised area of land, and a mound is a small one.
